arxiv-2104-09728.title: Production of dual species Bose-Einstein condensates of 39 K and 87 Rb
arxiv-2104-09728.creator: Cheng-Dong Mi, Khan Sadiq Nawaz, Peng-Jun Wang, Liang-Chao Chen, Zeng-ming Meng, Lianghui Huang, Jing Zhang
arxiv-2104-09728.description: Abstract We report the production of 39 K and 87 Rb Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs) in the lowest hyperfine states | F = 1 , m F = 1 ⟩ |F=1,m_{F}=1\rangle simultaneously. We collect atoms in bright/dark magneto-optical traps (MOTs) of 39 K/ 87 Rb to overcome the light-assisted losses of 39 K atoms.

arxiv-2507-02524.title: Time Resolution Independent Operator Learning
arxiv-2507-02524.creator: Diab W. Abueidda, Mbebo Nonna, Panos Pantidis, Mostafa E. Mobasher
arxiv-2507-02524.description: Abstract Accurately learning solution operators for time-dependent partial differential equations (PDEs) from sparse and irregular data remains a challenging task. Recurrent DeepONet extensions inherit the discrete-time limitations of sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) RNN architectures, while neural-ODE surrogates cannot incorporate new inputs after initialization.

arxiv-2510-14866.title: Benchmarking Multimodal Large Language Models for Face Recognition
arxiv-2510-14866.creator: Hatef Otroshi Shahreza, Sébastien Marcel
arxiv-2510-14866.description: Abstract Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have achieved remarkable performance across diverse vision-and-language tasks. However, their potential in face recognition remains underexplored. In particular, the performance of open-source MLLMs needs to be evaluated and compared with existing face recognition models on standard benchmarks with similar protocol.

arxiv-2512-20816.title: Infinitely many solutions and asymptotics for resonant oscillatory problems
arxiv-2512-20816.creator: Philip Korman Department of Mathematical Sciences University of Cincinnati Cincinnati Ohio 45221-0025 Dieter S. Schmidt Department of Computer Science University of Cincinnati Cincinnati, Ohio 45221-0030
arxiv-2512-20816.description: Abstract . For a class of oscillatory resonant problems, involving Dirichlet problems for semilinear PDE’s on balls and rectangles in R n R^{n} , we show the existence of infinitely many solutions, and study the global solution set. The first harmonic of the right hand side is not required to be zero, or small.

pmc-10648074.title: Exercise as a Promising Agent against Cancer: Evaluating Its Anti-Cancer Molecular Mechanisms
pmc-10648074.creator: Maria Spanoudaki, Constantinos Giaginis, Dimitra Karafyllaki, Konstantinos Papadopoulos, Evangelos Solovos, Georgios Antasouras, Georgios Sfikas, Athanasios N Papadopoulos, Sousana K Papadopoulou, Vasso Apostolopoulos, Tateaki Naito
pmc-10648074.description: Simple SummaryCancer is the main cause of mortality and morbidity worldwide. The incidence of physical inactivity is gradually increasing, reaching alarmingly high levels. Several review articles have summarized the potential beneficial effects of exercise in several aspects of the lifestyles of patients with cancer. However, only a few outdated review articles have focused on the anti-cancer molecular mechanisms of exercise.

pmc-11447933.title: Analysis of risk factors and construction of nomogram model for arthroscopic single-row rivet repair
pmc-11447933.creator: Hao Fan, YuLong Ouyang, ShuiLin Chen, DeFei Zhao, GuiCai Sun
pmc-11447933.description: BackgroundThe factors influencing the clinical outcome of arthroscopic rotator cuff repair are not fully understood.PurposeTo explore the factors related to the postoperative outcome of arthroscopic single-row rivet rotator cuff repair in patients with rotator cuff injury and to construct the related nomogram risk prediction model.Methods207 patients with rotator cuff injury who underwent arthroscopic single-row rivet rotator cuff repair were reviewed.

pmc-11481438.title: Comprehensive evaluation and guidance of structural variation detection tools in chicken whole genome sequence data
pmc-11481438.creator: Cheng Ma, Xian Shi, Xuzhen Li, Ya-Ping Zhang, Min-Sheng Peng
pmc-11481438.description: BackgroundStructural variations (SVs) are widespread across genome and have a great impact on evolution, disease, and phenotypic diversity. Despite the development of numerous bioinformatic tools, commonly referred to as SV callers, tailored for detecting SVs using whole genome sequence (WGS) data and employing diverse algorithms, their performance necessitates rigorous evaluation with real data and validated SVs.

pmc-11662444.title: Peroxisomal Localization of Benzyl Alcohol O-Benzoyltransferase HSR201 is Mediated by a Non-canonical Peroxisomal Targeting Signal and Required for Salicylic Acid Biosynthesis
pmc-11662444.creator: Yu Kotera, Yoshika Asai, Shutaro Okano, Yukako Tokutake, Akira Hosomi, Katsuharu Saito, Shinichi Yonekura, Shinpei Katou
pmc-11662444.description: The phytohormone salicylic acid (SA) regulates plant responses to various types of environmental stress, particularly pathogen infections. We previously revealed that the benzyl alcohol O-benzoyltransferase HSR201 was required for pathogen signal-induced SA synthesis, and its overexpression together with NtCNL, encoding a cinnamate-coenzyme A ligase, was sufficient for the production of significant amounts of SA in tobacco.

pmc-11713014.title: CSF biomarkers of immune activation and Alzheimer's disease for predicting cognitive impairment risk in the elderly

pmc-11713014.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe immune system is substantially involved in the development and progression of age‐related cognitive decline and Alzheimer’s disease (AD).MethodAs genetic and environmental factors interactively impact these conditions, we investigated how risk factors such as APOE genotype, age, and sex influence immune activation markers and AD biomarkers in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) in elderly individuals enrolled in the Mayo Clinic Study of Aging cohort.

pmc-12538449.title: Post-cholecystectomy bile acid diarrhea in a teenager with sickle cell disease: Case report
pmc-12538449.creator: Clarence Enerico Sumbizi, Orujul Hassan, Rashid Mbuma, Jackline Kifaluka, Athar Ali, Masawa Klint Nyamuryekung'e
pmc-12538449.description: Introduction and importanceBile acid diarrhea (BAD) caused by excessive bile acids entering the colon, is a frequently overlooked cause of chronic watery diarrhea, especially in the post-cholecystectomy setting. Although increasingly recognized in adults, its occurrence in the pediatric population is rare and underreported.

pmc-12653546.title: Objective Analysis of Reading Ability Using an Eye Tracker in Intermittent Exotropia
pmc-12653546.creator: Dong Hyun Kim, Jeong-Min Hwang, Hee Kyung Yang
pmc-12653546.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background/Objectives: This study’s objective was to analyze the reading ability in patients with intermittent exotropia using an eye tracker and determine how the clinical characteristics of intermittent exotropia may affect reading ability. Methods: We compared the reading speed (LPS; letters per second) of 25 intermittent exotropia patients to 25 age-matched normal controls who were 13 years old or older with best-corrected visual acuities of ≥20/25. Correlations between reading ability and clinical characteristics of intermittent exotropia were evaluated.

pmc-12723331.title: Efficient Capture of Short‐ and Long‐Chain PFAS from Water by a Metal–Organic Framework
pmc-12723331.creator: Thais Grancha, Patricia García‐Atienza, Lidia García, Sergio Armenta, José Manuel Herrero‐Martínez, Donatella Armentano, Teresa F Mastropietro, Jesús Ferrando Soria, Emilio Pardo
pmc-12723331.description: Per‐ and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), known as “forever chemicals,” present major environmental and health risks due to their extreme stability and dual hydrophobic–hydrophilic character, which complicates remediation. Conventional adsorbents such as activated carbon and ion‐exchange resins show limited performance, particularly for short‐chain PFAS.

pmc-13054852.title: Bridging Theory and Practice: a qualitative study on electronic charting and health systems science in Korean medicine education in alignment with KAS2022
pmc-13054852.creator: Won-Taek Lee, Bo-Min Kim, Ho-Yeon Choi, Seon-Kyoung Kim, Sang-Eun Park
pmc-13054852.description: ObjectivesThe digital transition in healthcare has underscored the importance of charting competence. However, medical record education remains fragmented and insufficient. With the introduction of competency-based assessments in KAS2022, there is an urgent need for structured training that integrates paper and electronic charts in Korean medicine education.MethodsThis qualitative study conducted focus group interviews with 19 students from a Korean medicine university.

pmc-13487926.title: Stem cell–based therapies in pediatric disorders: translational advances, unresolved challenges, and future horizons
pmc-13487926.creator: Hany E. Marei
pmc-13487926.description: Pediatric disorders consist of genetic, hematologic, neurologic, autoimmune, and inflammatory diseases. These conditions impose long-term health challenges on children, despite many advancements with conventional medicine. Although conventional treatments increase life expectancy and provide better disease control, many present challenges such as toxicity, insufficient control of the disease, and adverse effects on normal growth, development, and quality of life.

pmc-13571494.description: Accurate phenotypic acquisition determines the effectiveness of germplasm screening, while the efficiency and accuracy of image segmentation directly affect the quality of phenotypic parameter extraction.
